basis: Anterior displacement of the eye within the orbit defines this ocular disorder.
Immune-mediated cutaneous reaction; liver injury common (~60-80%); pneumonitis annotated 30-79%. Myocarditis and nephritis are occasional; delayed thyroid disease is separate.
Defines cardiac muscle and conduction disease. Skeletal myopathy is occasional; annotated lipodystrophy represents a separate LMNA-associated phenotype.
Centronuclear skeletal myopathy; dilated cardiomyopathy in 2/3 patients. Motor delay and respiratory weakness do not establish separate brain or lung damage.
Paralysis from motor-system dysfunction; classified under central nervous system disease. Weakness alone does not establish intrinsic muscle damage.
Malignant tumour originates in the pulmonary vein, a blood vessel; its name does not establish lung parenchymal involvement.
Visual-release hallucinations reflect neurologic dysfunction. The visual loss comes from a separate underlying eye, optic nerve or brain disorder.
Primary respiratory ciliary dysfunction; double-outlet right ventricle and recurrent middle-ear inflammation each reported in 2/2 patients; estimates have small denominators.
Lysosomal storage causes near-universal hepatic/splenic disease and common lung infiltration (>30%). Neurologic damage varies by subtype and is omitted under the four-axis cap.
Combined immunodeficiency with defining autoimmune cytopenias; hepatic nodular regenerative hyperplasia in 2/4. Bronchiectasis 1/5; infections and hypothyroidism are separate diseases.
Inherited dystonia is a neurologic movement disorder; spasms and tremor do not establish intrinsic muscle, eye or airway damage.
Congenital discontinuity of the aortic arch; associated cardiac defects remain within the cardiovascular axis.
Lymphoid-cell malignancy; lymphoma requires the infectious_immune mechanism axis. No additional organ is commonly directly involved.
Dysraphic lipomatous malformation occupies the conus of the spinal cord.
Disorder of the plantar fascia, a locomotor connective tissue; usual biomechanical degeneration does not establish an immune-mediated disease.
Digital malformations, microcephaly and gastrointestinal atresias are defining features; intellectual impairment ~51%. Cardiac, renal and hearing abnormalities are minorities.
Usher type I combines retinal rod-cone degeneration with congenital sensorineural deafness and vestibular dysfunction.
Irreversible generalized hair loss and cutaneous papular lesions define the disorder.
Both parents and synonyms define congenital pituitary hormone deficiency with microphthalmia.
Isolated male infertility from abnormal sperm flagella and motility; no endocrine dysfunction or other covered organ disease is established.
Congenital isolated growth hormone deficiency. Short stature reflects hormone deficiency; treatment-induced antibodies do not establish intrinsic immune disease.
Defined by a pathological postural fall in arterial blood pressure; an underlying neurologic cause is not universal.
Non-Hodgkin lymphoma is a lymphoid-cell malignancy; familial occurrence does not establish additional organ involvement.
Cardiac/skeletal malformations define major patterns; renal malformations annotated 80-99%, CNS defects 30-79% or higher. Ocular, otologic and palatal defects omitted at cap.
Skeletal-muscle channelopathy causing myotonia and painful contractions. Ocular paresis, dysphagia and hypothyroidism are occasional; potassium sensitivity is not a metabolic disorder.
